description:
The Paradox of Choice — explained in 60 seconds.

Beyond ~a handful of options, more choice creates paralysis and regret — not satisfaction.

What actually happens in your brain: Every option carries imagined trade-offs. With 57 choices, even a great pick feels like you lost 56 others.

Try it today: For big decisions, cut the menu to 3. 'Good enough' beats 'best' — because 'best' doesn't exist under 57 tabs.

narration: This one diagram explains your whole mood.
You probably believe this: MORE OPTIONS = MORE FREEDOM = MORE HAPPINESS. But that's not the full story.

Beyond about a handful of options, more choice creates paralysis and regret, not satisfaction. Here's what's happening: Every option carries imagined trade-offs. With 57 choices, even a great pick feels like you lost 56 others.
Iyengar & Lepper's jam study in 2000, 24 jam options drew more browsers; 6 options sold about 10x more.
For big decisions, cut the menu to 3. 'Good enough' beats 'best', because 'best' doesn't exist under 57 tabs. That's your Mindforge move for today. Follow for tomorrow's.
